# Live interoperability results

The [Live interop](https://github.com/thiagodefreitas/NetworkTime/blob/master/.github/workflows/interop.yml) workflow runs every Monday (and on demand)
on GitHub-hosted runners and queries public servers with every ntpstats client. The latest
results are in the workflow's job summary. Below is the first run, kept as a reference.

## 2026-09-29 11:26 UTC (ntpstats 2.2.0, GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`, IPv4)

### NTPv4 (SNTP, random transmit timestamp)

| server | address | stratum | refid | offset | delay | root dist. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| time.cloudflare.com | 162.159.200.123 | 3 | 10.157.8.4 | -65.6 µs | 5.15 ms | 6.1 ms |
| time.google.com | 216.239.35.0 | 1 | GOOG | -30.5 µs | 6.08 ms | 91.6 µs |
| ptbtime1.ptb.de | 192.53.103.108 | 1 | PTB | -121 µs | 93.7 ms | 68.7 µs |
| time.nist.gov | 132.163.97.4 | 1 | NIST | -1.85 ms | 47.1 ms | 610 µs |
| pool.ntp.org | 23.172.120.58 | 2 | 54.219.187.236 | -700 µs | 108 ms | 526 µs |
| ntp.ubuntu.com | 185.125.190.58 | 2 | 29.88.99.4 | -695 µs | 79 ms | 3.51 ms |

### NTS (RFC 8915): two authenticated exchanges per server

| server | NTP host:port | stratum | offset | delay | cookies left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| time.cloudflare.com | time.cloudflare.com:123 | 3 | -71.2 µs | 5.2 ms | 8 |
| nts.netnod.se | 194.58.205.197:4123 | 1 | -1.69 ms | 108 ms | 8 |
| ptbtime1.ptb.de | ptbtime1.ptb.de:123 | 1 | 474 µs | 95.9 ms | 8 |
| ntppool1.time.nl | ntppool1.time.nl:123 | 1 | 44 µs | 91.8 ms | 8 |
| ntp.3eck.net | ntp.3eck.net:123 | 2 | -525 µs | 95.6 ms | 8 |

Notes:
- Netnod hands out a different NTP server and port (4123) through the NTS-KE *server* and *port
  negotiation* records, which the client follows.
- "cookies left = 8" after two queries shows that cookie renewal works: each authenticated
  response returned a fresh cookie encrypted with the S2C key.
- The large offsets and delays of distant servers (PTB, Netnod and NIST seen from a US data
  centre) come from path asymmetry, not clock error. This is exactly what the offset/delay wedge
  and the delay-weighted estimators in ntpstats are for.

### NTPv5 (draft-ietf-ntp-ntpv5-09 upgrade probe)

None of the probed public servers (Cloudflare, PTB, time.nl) offered NTPv5 at the time of the
run. The v5 client is verified against a local draft-09 test server (see `tests/test_sntp.py`)
whose wire format was cross-checked with ntpd-rs.
